$comment: `required` is EMPTY on purpose, and the emptiness is the measurement. It listed all three fields until 2026-08-30, which made the honest answer unrepresentable: on the invoice-absent family both models omitted the field that was not in the document — the thing the system prompt asks for — and the schema rejected 6 of 10 as invalid. Two models with different capability scored identically (2/10) because the contract, not the model, was deciding. A missing field is now a legal answer and the exact-match oracle scores it; inventing 'N/A' or guessing a currency still scores wrong, which is the distinction worth keeping. `additionalProperties: false` is the other half: with an empty `required`, a schema that does not forbid undeclared keys accepts ANY object — MiniMax-M2.7 answered an invoice prompt with business_name and table_number and validated.
